This study introduces a relativistic coupled-cluster (CC) framework for calculating atomic energy levels, incorporating both the Breit interaction and electron correlation effects. The approach employs a relativistic coupled-cluster method with a single- and double-excitation approximation (CCSD) to model electron correlation, while the Breit interaction is treated as a perturbation. The resulting method, termed reaction relativistic coupled-cluster theory (R-RCCSD), is applied to indium isotopes to compute isotope shifts. The calculated isotope shifts align closely with experimental data, with a mean absolute deviation of 0.001 cm$^{-1}$, and the study also provides a detailed analysis of the contributions from various physical effects.

This study examines the principal minors of graphs, defined as the determinants of submatrices derived from the adjacency matrix. We demonstrate that these values are invariant under switching equivalence, a property that allows us to categorize graphs based on their principal minors. Our findings reveal that this categorization is highly effective for trees, uniquely identifying them up to isomorphism when the principal minors are known. Conversely, for general graphs, we provide examples of non-isomorphic graphs that share identical sets of principal minors.

This paper introduces a fundamental necessary condition for the presence of a transversal. While this condition is not sufficient on its own, it offers a practical method for determining non-existence. The authors demonstrate that their derived condition is logically equivalent to a well-known result by P. Hall regarding perfect matchings in bipartite graphs.

The escalating demand for high-quality video streaming has driven the adoption of transcoding services to optimize content for diverse devices and network conditions. However, transcoding is resource-intensive, making it essential to manage the trade-off between output quality and processing cost. This study introduces a framework for modeling and assessing video transcoding within heterogeneous cloud environments, specifically targeting the optimization of cost and quality. We propose a novel transcoding model that accounts for the specific characteristics of cloud providers and end-user devices. Furthermore, we develop a quality model to estimate the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) based on bitrate and resolution parameters. Utilizing this model, we formulate an optimization problem to determine the ideal transcoding configuration for a given input video. We validate our approach through experiments using real-world video files and data from major cloud providers, including Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, and Microsoft Azure. The results demonstrate that our proposed model effectively identifies the most cost-effective transcoding settings for various input videos.

This study examines the impact of cycle count variations on the performance of the Intel Xeon Phi coprocessor. The authors demonstrate that for specific applications, performance can fluctuate by as much as 20% due to minor shifts in instruction cycle counts, which are often negligible. The research further indicates that these fluctuations are primarily driven by the processor's branch prediction mechanisms.

This study examines the ground state of the energy ultracritical Gross--Pitaevskii equation, which is defined as the energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with a delta potential centered at the origin. We demonstrate that the ground state possesses a finite Morse index.

This study introduces a formal framework for managing Type I errors in automated design evaluation, a critical issue for the emerging field of automated design. The proposed methodology is versatile, accommodating both single and multi-objective design scenarios. It establishes a formal basis for defining the design space and the corresponding null hypothesis, enabling the application of standard statistical significance testing. The paper outlines the theoretical underpinnings of this framework and illustrates its practical utility through a case study involving the automated optimization of a 3D printed structure.

The rapid advancement of virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) has created a demand for immersive, high-fidelity visual experiences. However, rendering these scenes in real-time remains a significant challenge due to the vast scale of the required 3D models and textures. To address this, we introduce a distributed hybrid rendering framework that leverages both client-side and server-side resources to enhance performance. By utilizing a server to handle the rendering of distant objects, we significantly reduce the computational load on the client device. Furthermore, we employ a novel hybrid rendering technique that combines rasterization with ray tracing to achieve both high efficiency and visual fidelity. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach delivers superior rendering quality while maintaining high performance.

This study examines the annotation and alignment accuracy of various deep learning models designed for complex orchestral music. We introduce a new dataset featuring 100 pieces of such music, annotated with high precision by professional musicians. The study also presents a novel evaluation metric that leverages these precise annotations to assess model performance. Our findings indicate that while current deep learning models achieve high accuracy in detecting note onsets and offsets, they struggle with alignment precision in intricate musical contexts.

However, their widespread adoption is hindered by self-interference (SI), which arises from the leakage of a transmitter's own signal into its receiver. This paper presents a novel framework for SI suppression in FDRs, integrating a multiantenna architecture with a hybrid analog-to-digital beamforming approach. This study investigates the buckling and infolding of colloidal droplets, which are formed by the aggregation of smaller droplets. We demonstrate that the infolding mechanism is governed by the interplay between surface tension and the bending rigidity of the resulting colloidal film. By analyzing the equilibrium configuration of the infolded droplet, we establish a relationship between the infolding radius and the aggregate's volume. Furthermore, we examine the kinetics of the infolding process, identifying a transition from a diffusion-controlled to a reaction-controlled regime. Finally, we propose a theoretical model that accurately describes the time-dependent evolution of the infolding radius.

We present a novel method for determining the age of protoplanetary disks by analyzing the evolution of their Lyman-alpha (LyA) and ultraviolet (UV) emission. This approach relies on the fact that UV radiation from the central star is absorbed by hydrogen gas in the disk, creating a fluorescent response that tracks the disk's gas content. As the disk evolves, the gas density drops, causing the UV flux to rise. This increase is detectable through the LyA line, which exhibits a characteristic double-peaked profile. The ratio of the LyA line flux to the continuum UV flux serves as a reliable age indicator, as it is largely independent of the disk's inclination and the central star's luminosity. We demonstrate that this ratio increases by a factor of 100 over the first 10 million years of a disk's life. Furthermore, we show that the LyA line profile can be used to estimate the disk's inclination, allowing for the derivation of the central star's luminosity and the subsequent calculation of the disk's age. This technique is applicable to a wide range of protoplanetary disks, including those with low gas densities.

This paper introduces a fingerprint-based millimeter-wave (mmWave) localization framework that leverages reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to enhance positioning accuracy. The study first establishes a mmWave channel model incorporating RIS, followed by the development of a channel state information (CSI) acquisition protocol. Subsequently, a positioning methodology utilizing CSI is proposed, which involves constructing a database of fingerprints from the mmWave-RIS channel and employing a nearest-neighbor search algorithm to determine user locations. The efficacy of this approach is validated through simulations, demonstrating that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy compared to existing solutions.

We examine the generation of twisted particles within a uniform magnetic field, demonstrating that the polarization vector acquires a geometric phase contingent upon the particle's spin. This phenomenon is illustrated by showing that circularly polarized photons in such a field acquire orbital angular momentum, becoming vortex photons. Furthermore, we establish that the photon's angular momentum is transferred to the field, resulting in the field's vortex formation.

This study examines the economic and engineering design of electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, specifically focusing on the optimal siting of charging stations and the pricing of electricity and ancillary services. The research addresses the challenges of integrating EVs into the power grid, which is complicated by the diverse and uncertain charging behaviors of individual vehicles. To tackle this, the authors develop a comprehensive framework that incorporates both the charging station operator's and the grid operator's perspectives. The operator's objective is to maximize profit by determining the ideal number and location of stations, as well as setting prices for electricity and ancillary services. The grid operator's objective is to minimize total system costs by managing the dispatch of generation and transmission assets. The study also analyzes the market mechanisms required to achieve these goals, including the design of a market for ancillary services. The authors demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively address the challenges of integrating EVs into the power grid.

This study introduces a unified framework for analyzing tie-breaker experiments, specifically focusing on the optimal allocation of treatments. We establish that the optimal design for experiments with potential ties is equivalent to the optimal design for experiments without ties, provided the latter accounts for a specific expanded treatment category. Additionally, we offer a practical method for calculating this optimal expanded treatment design, which is demonstrated through its application to a study on the impact of class size on student achievement.

This study examines three-point correlation functions involving spinor current multiplets of arbitrary higher spin within ${\mathcal N}=1$ superconformal field theories. We derive a general formula for these correlations, which is expressed through a set of coefficients that are fixed by the superconformal algebra. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these three-point functions can be constructed from a single integral expression, with the integrand being a product of three delta functions.

Children's fascination with how computers function is well-documented, yet the specific aspects of computing that captivate them remains an under-researched area. This study investigates the interest of children aged 8 to 12 in machine-level operations. We conducted semi-structured interviews with 16 participants to assess their understanding of machine instructions and their ability to create machine-level programs. The findings reveal that these participants possess a rudimentary grasp of machine instructions and demonstrate a desire to explore them further.

This paper examines enduring reinforcement learning (RL) systems, defined as those that persist indefinitely without requiring human intervention. We present a comprehensive review of existing literature, focusing on the specific challenges and hurdles faced by these enduring systems. Our analysis reveals that while current RL methods are effective for short-term tasks, they often fail to meet the demands of long-term applications. We propose a framework for categorizing RL systems based on their duration and identify the unique obstacles associated with each type. Our findings indicate that enduring systems face distinct challenges that are not adequately addressed by current research. We outline a set of critical research directions to advance the field of enduring RL systems, emphasizing the need for a more comprehensive understanding of long-term dynamics.

We present an integrated optical platform designed for the coherent conversion of quantum information between distinct photonic properties, specifically utilizing the trade-off between spatial mode and frequency. This system employs a tunable array of waveguide resonators to achieve such transformations. We demonstrate that this approach facilitates the generation of frequency-bin entanglement from spatially mode-entangled light and vice versa. Furthermore, we illustrate that the platform can support quantum teleportation across these different degrees of freedom.

This study investigates the quantum transport characteristics of DNA strands featuring mismatched base pairs. By employing a tight-binding model, we examine how the spatial arrangement of mispairs influences transport behavior. Our findings indicate that the conductance of DNA with mispairs is significantly lower than that of perfect sequences, a result that aligns with experimental observations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the conductance of defective DNA is highly sensitive to the applied bias voltage, exhibiting a complex, non-monotonic pattern. Additionally, we observe that the conductance of DNA with mispairs is strongly dependent on temperature, a feature that can be explained by the emergence of a Kondo effect.

This paper introduces a new method for efficiently and robustly registering multiple point clouds. The approach begins by applying K-means clustering to group the point clouds, followed by the application of the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm to register these groups. The resulting registered point clouds are then clustered again using K-means, and the ICP algorithm is executed once more to register these new clusters. This process repeats until the ICP algorithm converges. The method's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This study examines the magnetic architecture of Tb$_3$RuO$_7$, a material characterized by alternating Ru spin-3/2 chains and Tb$^{3+}$ ions. The Tb$^{3+}$ ions generate a non-uniform internal magnetic field that acts upon the Ru chains, inducing a complex magnetic phase diagram. At low temperatures, the system exhibits a partially disordered state where the Ru chains alternate between two distinct magnetic configurations: one with a ferromagnetic ground state and another with a spin-glass-like ground state. This alternating pattern is dictated by the specific arrangement of Tb$^{3+}$ ions.

This study examines necessary optimality criteria within the framework of direct current (DC) constrained mathematical programming. We introduce novel concepts of stationary points specifically tailored to DC problems and demonstrate that every local minimizer satisfies these conditions. Furthermore, we establish necessary optimality conditions under the assumption of an appropriate second-order sufficient condition.

We investigate the dynamics of fundamental strings in the near-horizon limit of the D$(-1)/$D7 brane system, which corresponds to the near-horizon geometry of D$(-1)$ branes embedded in a D$7$ background. This geometry is identified as AdS$_1$ with a time-like boundary, accompanied by a non-trivial dilaton and Kalb-Ramond fields. We demonstrate that the string's worldsheet theory is dual to a specific quantum mechanical system. Furthermore, we analyze the spectrum of this worldsheet theory and its dual quantum mechanical counterpart, confirming that their energy levels align perfectly.

Domain clashes represent a specific type of conflict that occurs when a domain name is registered by an unauthorized third party. This issue is particularly prevalent in the context of the Internet, where such clashes can lead to significant legal and practical complications. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the various forms of domain clashes, examines the legal frameworks governing them, and discusses the different resolution mechanisms available.

This study introduces a new method for incorporating controllers into deep reinforcement learning (RL) systems, specifically designed to enhance sample efficiency and accelerate learning. We achieve this by embedding control priors directly into the RL policy architecture, a process that remains fully Bayesian and requires no hyperparameter tuning. Our approach is versatile, supporting both model-free and model-based RL, as well as continuous and discrete action spaces. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness through experiments on two robotics tasks: a simulated robotic arm reaching task and a real-world quadruped robot walking.

Perfusion imaging is a critical component of acute stroke management, enabling clinicians to evaluate cerebral blood flow and volume. This process typically involves applying deconvolution to perfusion maps to derive the cerebral blood flow (CBF) impulse response function (IRF). However, conventional methods rely on the Laplace transform, which is non-differentiable and prevents the use of gradient-based optimization. This study introduces a differentiable deconvolution technique that enables gradient computation for the CBF IRF. By integrating this approach into a differentiable imaging pipeline, we can optimize IRF parameters to maximize the likelihood of stroke territory identification. Experimental results demonstrate that our method yields IRFs with higher signal-to-noise ratios and greater accuracy in delineating stroke regions compared to standard Laplace transform approaches.

We present the first next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) analytic expressions for jet and groomed jet functions within the framework of zero-jettiness effective field theory. These results are derived using the method of soft-collinear subtractions and are applicable to both soft-drop and m-$\beta$ angular-ordered grooming algorithms. By establishing these functions, we enable the calculation of differential cross sections for jet observables at N$^3$LO accuracy.

A finite group $G$ is defined as chordal if its power graph, $W(G)$, exhibits a chordal graph structure. This paper establishes that the power graph of a finite group $G$ is chordal if and only if $G$ is either a finite $p$-group or a finite cyclic group of order $p^nq$ (where $p$ and $q$ are prime numbers).

This study addresses the challenge of separating target sources from noisy environments. We introduce a new training strategy that utilizes a synthetic environment to enhance the model's ability to generalize to unseen real-world conditions. Our approach involves training the model on a dataset where the environment is generated synthetically, allowing for precise control over the target source and background noise. We demonstrate that this method significantly improves performance on real-world data compared to training solely on observed data. Our results show that the model trained with synthetic environments achieves superior performance on real-world data compared to training solely on observed data.

We introduce a new framework for analyzing consistency across quantum measurements, a concept that extends the established definition of consistency regarding quantum states. This novel approach enables the detection of consistency relative to broader classes of measurements, including those that are non-projective. Furthermore, we demonstrate that consistency within this specific framework is equivalent to measurement independence.

We report the detection of Type C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the X-ray transient H 1743–322 during two distinct outbursts, utilizing data from the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RXTE) and the Swift/X-ray Telescope (XRT). The RXTE observations reveal a QPO with a period of 1.12 ± 0.02 s, while the Swift/XRT data show a QPO with a period of 1.13 ± 0.03 s. These findings indicate that the QPOs in H 1743–322 are consistent with the type C class. Furthermore, the QPOs observed in Swift/XRT data are characterized by a low root-mean-square (rms) amplitude of 1.1 ± 0.1% and a high coherence of 0.93 ± 0.03. These characteristics suggest that the QPOs in H 1743–322 are generated by a stable accretion flow.

This paper introduces an open-domain Question Answering (QA) system designed to enhance e-governance by addressing the limitations of current government portals, which often rely on rigid, form-based interactions that are difficult for the general public to navigate. We developed a natural language interface that leverages a QA model trained on a dataset of queries and responses collected from the Indian government. This system is built upon a modular architecture featuring a modular backend that integrates a Natural Language Processing (NLP) model, a REST API, and a frontend. The NLP component utilizes a fine-tuned BERT model to deliver precise answers to user inquiries.

This study investigates the baryon budget within the EAGLE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, which are among the most advanced tools for modeling galaxy formation. We analyze the baryon budget across various mass scales, from the smallest resolved structures to the largest cosmological volumes. Our findings indicate that the missing baryons are predominantly located in the intergalactic medium (IGM) and are largely unaccounted for in current observational surveys. We demonstrate that the baryon budget is highly sensitive to the resolution of the simulation, with a significant fraction of baryons residing in unresolved dark matter halos. A "leftmost $i$-divider" of a string $S$ is defined as the earliest occurrence of a character in $S$ that splits $S$ into two parts with no common characters. This paper introduces a new algorithm capable of identifying all such dividers for any given $k \geq 0$. The method runs in $O(nk)$ time and $O(k)$ space, where $n$ represents the string's length. Additionally, we demonstrate that this approach is optimal for the RAM model with word size $O(\log n)$, provided $k$ is at least $\Omega(n/\log n)$.

We investigate the stellar velocity dispersion ($\sigma$) and central velocity offset ($\Delta V$) in 1,000 galaxies from the SDSS-III MaNGA survey, focusing on those with post-starburst (PSB) or quiescent (QSO) properties. These samples are defined by strong Balmer absorption lines and a lack of H$\alpha$ emission. Our analysis reveals that PSB galaxies exhibit a median $\sigma$ of $100$ km s$^{-1}$ and a median $\Delta V$ of $10$ km s$^{-1}$, while QSO galaxies show a median $\sigma$ of $110$ km s$^{-1}$ and a median $\Delta V$ of $20$ km s$^{-1}$. The $\Delta V$ distribution for PSB galaxies is notably narrower than that of QSO galaxies. Furthermore, the $\Delta V$ distribution for PSB galaxies is significantly more concentrated around zero compared to the QSO distribution. We also examine the relationship between $\Delta V$ and $\sigma$, finding that the $\Delta V$-$\sigma$ relation for PSB galaxies is steeper than that for QSO galaxies. Reconfigurable wireless networks (RWNs) are designed to adapt their topology and communication protocols to meet the diverse needs of various applications. However, the dynamic nature of these networks introduces significant challenges for scheduling, particularly regarding the trade-off between Quality of Service (QoS) and energy efficiency. This paper introduces a novel QoS-aware scheduler for RWNs that leverages the synergy between a performer and a critic within a reinforcement learning framework. The proposed method utilizes a critic to forecast the QoS levels of potential schedulings, thereby guiding the performer to select actions that maximize QoS while minimizing energy consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both QoS and energy efficiency.

We introduce a method for estimating word-level accuracy in machine translation (MT) outputs, designed to support post-editing assistance. This approach utilizes a pre-existing MT system's confidence scores and the frequency of source and target words to calculate individual word accuracies. These estimations are then applied to help post-editors by highlighting the specific words that require the most attention. We demonstrate the method's effectiveness through a user study involving German-to-English translation, where our system successfully identified the most critical words for editing.

This study investigates the silhouette of a Kerr-de Sitter black hole, defined as the boundary of its shadow, to determine the values of the cosmological constant. We demonstrate that this constant can be estimated with high precision by analyzing the shadow's radius and the inclination angle of the observer. Furthermore, we examine how the shadow's shape varies in response to changes in the cosmological constant and the black hole's spin.

This study introduces a novel formulation of relativistic hydrodynamics equations in two-dimensional Cartesian coordinates, designed to facilitate the development of numerical schemes for simulating relativistic fluid flows. This study presents a search for the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ mesons, where $J$ represents the spin, in the decay channels $D^{*+} K^0_{\rm S}$ and $D^{*0} K^+$. The analysis utilizes data from the LHCb experiment, collected with the LHCb detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $1.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ at a center-of-mass energy of $7\,\text{TeV}$. The investigation focuses on the $D^{(*)+}_{sJ}$ states with masses between $2.0$ and $2.5\,\text{GeV}/c^2$ and spins of $0$ or $1$. No significant signals are observed for these states, leading to the establishment of upper limits on the product of the branching fraction and production cross-section for the $D^{*+}_{sJ}$ mesons.

This paper introduces a novel class of fractal polynomials defined on the Sierpiński gasket, an iconic example of a fractal set. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to a specific functional equation involving three arbitrary complex parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these fractal polynomials are continuous and possess a unique property of self-similarity. Additionally, we prove that they are not bounded and do not converge in the uniform norm.

Visual Question Answering (VQA) systems are trained to address inquiries about images, yet current datasets often suffer from a lack of diversity in question types, which hinders the model's ability to generalize. To address this, we introduce a method for generating questions that are both diverse and semantically aligned with specific images. Our approach utilizes a two-stage pipeline: first, a language model generates candidate questions based on image captions, and second, a reinforcement learning agent refines these to produce questions that are diverse and relevant. We evaluate our method using a human-annotated benchmark and demonstrate that it successfully creates a wide array of question types, including those that are challenging.

The cusp-core transformation (CCT) involves a shift from a central density cusp to a flatter core within a dark matter halo. While the prevailing explanation attributes this to the gravitational feedback from supernovae (SN) ejecting low-mass stars, this mechanism faces significant challenges. Specifically, it requires an SN energy output roughly 100 times greater than the gravitational binding energy of the halo to achieve the necessary mass ejection, a scenario that is physically implausible. Furthermore, the SN-driven process is inherently inefficient because it ejects stars across a broad mass spectrum rather than targeting low-mass ones. Consequently, this study argues that the SN-driven mechanism is unlikely to be the primary driver of the CCT.

This paper introduces novel advanced variable elimination techniques derived from the theory of modern SAT solvers. These methods are straightforward to implement and integrate into existing CDCL SAT solvers with minimal disruption. We detail the specific properties of each method and provide experimental results demonstrating their performance.

This study examines the replicator equation, a mathematical framework for modeling evolutionary dynamics, by applying similarity-order preserving mappings (SOPMs) to its right-hand side. These mappings are defined by their ability to maintain the relative ordering of values while ensuring the sum of the resulting vector components equals zero. We demonstrate that SOPMs applied to the replicator equation generate a system with a stable equilibrium, where the final state depends on the initial conditions. Furthermore, the paper explores the historical behavior of the system, revealing that the trajectory of the evolution is determined by the specific SOPM employed. These findings suggest that the replicator equation, when coupled with SOPMs, offers a versatile model for understanding various evolutionary processes.

This paper establishes a novel asymptotic typicality theorem for multivariate random forest estimators, which serves as a functional counterpart to the classical notion of typicality in information theory. We demonstrate that, as the sample size grows, the empirical typicality matrix of a random forest estimator converges in probability to a deterministic limit. This result is pivotal for addressing the issue of generalization in machine learning, as it enables the derivation of a bound on the expected generalization error.

This study addresses electric vehicle (EV) charging within unbalanced distribution grids, aiming to minimize power losses and voltage deviations while ensuring voltage limits are met. The problem is formulated as a non-convex optimization task, which is then linearized to create a convex approximation. To solve this, we introduce a distributed algorithm that relies on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), utilizing only local data and limited communication between adjacent nodes. The proposed method is validated through simulations on a 13-node unbalanced test feeder, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing voltage violations and power losses.

The structural, electronic, and elastic properties of the rare-earth manganite $SmFeO_3$ were investigated using the density functional theory (DFT) within the generalized gradient approximation (GGA). The study confirms that the material crystallizes in an orthorhombic perovskite structure, characterized by a $Pnma$ space group. The calculated lattice parameters align well with experimental data. Furthermore, the computed bulk modulus, shear modulus, and Young's modulus are in good agreement with available experimental values. The material exhibits a band gap of 2.11 eV, indicating semiconducting behavior. Additionally, the calculated Poisson's ratio of 0.25 suggests that $SmFeO_3$ possesses ductile characteristics.

Bacterial genomes are highly diverse, yet they share a common set of essential genes that encode the machinery required for survival. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of 1,000 bacterial genomes, identifying 1,050 core genes and reconstructing 250 metabolic pathways. By examining the evolutionary history of these pathways, we discovered that while most are ancient, a few are relatively recent additions. Furthermore, we identified a strong correlation between the presence of specific pathways and the ecological niches bacteria inhabit. This research provides a foundational framework for investigating the evolution of metabolic pathways and their adaptation to different environments.

This study introduces a data-driven modeling approach for the ventilation subsystem within a smart building, utilizing a Bayesian framework to integrate sensor data with physical principles. The model incorporates a probabilistic representation of the ventilation subsystem alongside a probabilistic description of the building's occupancy. By employing a variational inference algorithm, the model estimates the posterior distribution of occupancy counts, which are then used to dynamically adjust ventilation airflow rates. The proposed method is validated using data from a real smart building, demonstrating its effectiveness.

We present a detailed analysis of the Type Ic supernova SN 2017gci, which is the most luminous and longest-lasting Type Ic event recorded to date. Its peak absolute magnitude reached $M_{\rm V} = -20.1$ mag, and it remained visible in the optical spectrum for 300 days. The light curve exhibits a prolonged plateau phase lasting approximately 100 days, followed by a gradual decline. The spectral evolution reveals a distinct transition from a broad-lined Type Ic to a Type Ib-like appearance. We propose that SN 2017gci resulted from the merger of two massive stars, which created a hybrid progenitor system. This system likely consisted of a helium core with a hydrogen-rich envelope, a configuration that accounts for the observed spectral shift. The event's extreme luminosity and prolonged duration are attributed to the interaction between the hydrogen envelope and the helium core, which generated a substantial amount of radioactive $^{56}\rm{Ni}$. Theoretical models indicate that the progenitor's mass was approximately $100\rm{M}_{\odot}$, with a hydrogen mass fraction of $X_{\rm H} \approx 0.01$.

We examine the quantum dynamics of a single-domain magnet, focusing on the interplay between the exchange field and thermal fluctuations. By analyzing the magnetization reversal of a two-dimensional Ising ferromagnet, we demonstrate that the magnetization reversal rate is governed by the ratio of the exchange field to thermal fluctuations. This relationship is expressed through a quantum Stoner-Wohlfarth theory, which establishes a universal scaling law for the magnetization reversal rate. This scaling law is validated by numerical simulations of a two-dimensional Ising ferromagnet, as well as experimental data from a two-dimensional ferromagnetic van der Waals material.

Dependency parsing is a fundamental natural language processing task that involves identifying binary relations between words. While recent advancements have largely focused on refining the induction of these relations, this study introduces a novel approach to modeling them. We propose a new dependency type called "visual dependency," which is derived from the visual perception of a sentence's dependency parse tree. This concept is grounded in the theory that humans visually perceive syntactic structures, a process that has been extensively researched in cognitive science. By leveraging visual perception, we can capture the inherent hierarchical nature of sentences, thereby enhancing the modeling of dependencies. Consequently, we have developed a new dependency type system based on visual perception and constructed a corresponding treebank. Experimental results demonstrate that utilizing this visual dependency type system significantly improves dependency parsing performance.

This study evaluates the performance of various feature attribution techniques by comparing their outputs with ground-truth semantic masks. We introduce a novel metric, the Feature Attribution Error (FAE), to quantify the discrepancy between attribution maps and actual semantic masks. Our analysis reveals that the performance ranking of these methods varies significantly depending on the specific task and dataset. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the FAE metric effectively captures the performance degradation caused by the removal of features.

This study examines the linearization stability of a specific class of thin-shell wormholes featuring reflection asymmetry and double photon regions. We demonstrate that the linearization stability condition for these asymmetric double-shadow structures is mathematically equivalent to the condition found in spherically symmetric cases with a single photon sphere. Consequently, the previously established lower bounds for the throat radius in double-shadow thin-shell wormholes with spherical symmetry remain valid for this broader asymmetric category.
